evidence.note: Original UP Medford Mail Tribune July 21, 1948 p1 names Henry Winston among six New York defendants arrested last night. July 20 arrest belongs to the Smith Act prosecution, not his later 1956 surrender. Original scan visually inspected. Earlier duplicate populated July 19 remains untouched.

Original UP H. D. Quigg report, Bend Bulletin October 21, 1949 p1, individually names Winston among ten five-year sentences imposed today. Original scan visually inspected. Existing 1956 incarceration and 1961 release retained; sentencing does not imply confinement in 1949. Duplicate populated October 20 remains untouched.

Francis Gorgen firsthand letter, Catholic Worker September 1959 printed pp4-5, visually inspected: Monday August 24 Omaha action, 10:55 US Marshal arrest, court that afternoon, Judge Richard Robinson six months and immediate county-jail confinement. Quoted docket explicitly August 24. Existing arrest YEAR 1959 and its precision preserved; no day refinement of populated arrest.

Ammon Hennacy own Life in Sandstone Prison, Catholic Worker February 1960 printed p3, visually inspected: expressly released from Sandstone January 20th, met Dorothy and Francis on release, onward travel described. January 24 elsewhere in issue concerns a CBS telecast, not release. Own actual release, not a projected good-time estimate. Other cases untouched.

Robert Lax original archival photograph DD#10, DD-CW W-8 Box 2, caption transcribed by Dorothy Day biographer Jim Forest: Dorothy entering police wagon after civil-defense drill arrest, Washington Square Park July 20, 1956. Marquette collection independently identifies same demonstration and person. Already populated custody endpoints and portrait preserved; this photograph is evidence only, not a replacement image.

Ammon Hennacy In the Market Place, Catholic Worker February 1957 printed p2, visually inspected: in court on the 15th before Judge Comerford concerning guilty pleas last July; $25 or five days, with Dorothy own court statement separately named. January 15 sentencing belongs to this already dated sentence-serving row. Do not invent a fresh January arrest or merge with the separate July 1956 arrest row.

Original National Guardian July 22, 1957 printed p2, visually inspected, names Dorothy Day among ten peaceful protesters arrested Friday July 12 at Sarah Delano Roosevelt Park. Not a later Times Square hearing for Richard and Jane Moses.

Participant Karl Meyer own Sixty Years with The Catholic Worker memoir, first published June/July 2017 and reproduced by NWTRCC February/March 2018: specifically July 12, 1957 action with Dorothy and Ammon, overnight Tombs custody, all sentenced to thirty days in court next day. July 13 derived from that explicit next-day chronology; contemporary Guardian independently confirms thirty-day sentences. Existing release August 6 retained; no sentence-length arithmetic substituted for discharge.

Marquette custodian of Dorothy Day papers explicitly dates her fifth and last drill arrest April 17, 1959 and identifies Vivian Cherry photograph just before that arrest. Initial arrest row already has April 17 confinement; fill missing arrest only. Do not invent release across the interval before her later court appearance.

Dorothy Day On Pilgrimage July 1959 reproduces commanding officer Court Detention Pens Manhattan report: received Friday April 24, 1959, sentenced $25 or ten days by Magistrate Roe. Exact court report distinguishes sentencing from earlier April 17 arrest. Existing April 24 confinement and May 4 release preserved; separate initial-arrest row retained.

Original UP Medford Mail Tribune May 21, 1948 p1, visually inspected: Hollywood Movie Writers Sentenced, Washington May 21 dateline, John Howard Lawson and Dalton Trumbo each sentenced today to one year. Both remain free on bond pending appeal. Sentencing precedes actual 1950 prison admission; no arrest inferred from HUAC testimony, subpoena, indictment or verdict.

Original AP Bend Bulletin June 29, 1950 printed p8, visually inspected: Six Hollywood Men Sentenced expressly names Albert Maltz among defendants sentenced today. No arrest inferred from sentence or admission. Article contradictory Scott line is not reused for Scott; existing Maltz confinement and release retained.

Original AP Washington June 29 dateline, Scurry County Times June 30, 1950 printed p5/PDF5, full page and article detail visually inspected: names writer-director Biberman among six sentenced today, while Scott and Ornitz deferred. Printed first name Herman is a newspaper error; surname, Hollywood Ten prosecution and director role identify Herbert. Article also inaccurately generalizes one-year terms, so no term or fine copied.

Original National Guardian July 5, 1950 printed p6, visually inspected, independently names Herbert Biberman among six sentenced the preceding week and distinguishes six-month sentence. Cross-check identity only; existing sentence prose and populated dates/precision remain unchanged.
